claims.statement: Clauset Shalizi Newman paper Power-Law Distributions in Empirical Data appeared SIAM Review 51(4):661-703 electronically 6 Nov 2009
claims.locator: p661 copyright metadata and online date

claims.statement: 2009 paper organizes maximum likelihood threshold estimation, KS semiparametric bootstrap goodness of fit, and likelihood ratio comparison with rivals
Power law may hold only for x>=xmin; continuous density (alpha-1)/xmin*(x/xmin)^(-alpha) alpha>1
Continuous-tail power law MLE alpha_hat=1+n/sum ln(x_i/xmin) for n qualifying independent observations
Discrete degree-tail distribution uses x^-alpha/zeta(alpha,xmin), not naive continuous MLE
Choose xmin by minimizing KS distance between empirical CDF and fitted model in selected tail
Goodness of fit simulates synthetic data under fitted law and compares corresponding KS distances to empirical distance
Paper proposes p>0.1 as plausible and smaller p as rejection, not posterior probability law is true
Paper compares exponential, lognormal, stretched exponential and cutoff power-law alternatives with likelihood ratio methods
Of 24 empirical datasets, 17 were consistent with power law under goodness of fit and seven rejected, while competitor comparisons yield more qualified conclusions
claims.locator: pp681-685 section6 and Table3; p688 Table5

claims.statement: If PMF density tail decays k^-alpha with alpha>1, CCDF has asymptotic exponent alpha-1
Goodness of fit not rejection does not establish unique truth or generating causal mechanism and finite-sample statistical power matters
1998 clustering/path question, 1999 hub formation model, 2009 evidence testing are distinct and do not establish navigability in Kleinberg's 2000 sense
